Metistry Design System

3.2 Activity Feed Rows

Real kinds from the activity_feed query. Agent actors carry the agent tint; a failure tints the detail line, never the whole row. Subjects are Title Cased at render (§3.2) — but only for kinds the console itself composes. The first two rows are tool and dispatch, whose subjects can carry agent-authored text: they render exactly as stored, identifiers and all, because agent text is data and data is not case-corrected (P1). Detail lines stay sentence case throughout — they are prose (P10).

3.4 · 3.5 · 4 Chat Turn, Reply Text, Collapsed Tool Activity, Prompt Card

The reply below is ~180 words in the §4 reply tokens — 15pt on a phone, 16pt on a Mac, line 1.45, 12px between paragraphs instead of a blank line, 4px between list items. Read it on the phone: dense enough that the turn above is still on screen, comfortable enough to read to the end. Nothing here uses --mt-text-body-*; those are control tokens. The disclosure is a native <details>, and everything inside the agent wash is agent-sourced data.

Light
you · 09:14
how much should I ease off running in the final weeks?
assistant · 09:14 · finished · deep · 6.2s

Cut total weekly volume by about 40% across the final three weeks and hold intensity where it is. A taper sheds fatigue, not fitness — dropping the hard sessions is the mistake that actually costs you the race, and it is the one nearly everybody makes.

  • Three weeks out — keep the long run, cap it at 90 minutes; one interval session at race pace, half the usual volume.
  • Two weeks out — about 60% of peak mileage. The last genuinely hard session lands here, ten days from the start.
  • Race week — 30 to 40% of peak. Two easy runs, four strides on the Thursday, and nothing at all on the Saturday.

Your note Areas/Running/Taper already puts the last hard session ten days out, so this only sharpens what is there. Weekly totals, kilometres:

peak 68 · w-3 41 · w-2 27 · race wk 24

One caveat, and it comes from the health collector rather than the training log: your average sleep is down 44 minutes on the same block last year, and fatigue you have not recovered from does not care what week the plan says it is. Err toward the low end of every number above.

3.6 Composer Actions Menu

Nothing but the composer occupies the space above the keyboard — a pinned command strip costs two or three lines of transcript exactly while you are typing about what the agent just said (P8, P9). One ＋ holds the lot, and the list under it is generated from live rules.yaml and the agent registry, never hand-maintained. On the web it is a native <details>: it opens with no script, is keyboard-operable, and Esc closes it. Every item in the menu is clickable and inserts itself at the caret — it never sends, so a tapped command and a typed one produce the identical string. The third state below is suggesting: typing @d or / opens the same generated list as an inline listbox under the field, ranked prefix → substring → recency, driven by ↑↓ / Enter / Esc.

3.6 · 3.7 The ⌘K Palette and the Model & Effort Picker

⌘K stays, and it is the rich reply surface wherever a desktop keyboard is present. The inline suggestion list above is the narrow affordance — six rows, one token, right for a thumb. The palette is the wide one: it searches all four groups at once with the same deterministic ranking, shows the full description and the shortcut, previews an agent's presence before you address it, and stays open across several insertions so a turn can be composed from a command, an agent and a model pin without reopening anything. Results insert at the caret exactly as the menu's do. Shown only where (pointer: fine) matches — never on touch, where it would be a shortcut with no keyboard. The picker is a human override of a deterministic router (invariant 4), and its header says so.

3.17 Destructive Confirmation

The dialog is never the control — the server refuses regardless. It exists so the click is not cheaper than the act, and it always names the consequence.

Light
Rotate the token for ops-bot?

The current token stops working immediately. Anything still using it will start failing authentication until you paste the new one. The new token is shown once and never again.

Dark
Rotate the token for ops-bot?

The current token stops working immediately. Anything still using it will start failing authentication until you paste the new one. The new token is shown once and never again.

5 Wireframes

One architecture, three renderings. Every screen is an annotated SVG in this directory — text-editable, tokens as literal values, numbered red callouts and a legend. Links rather than embeds, so this page stays self-contained. The navigation in all of them is the six sections (Chat · Feed · Work▸ · Knowledge▸ · Agents · Insights) plus Pinned on the Mac, with capture as a floating ＋ and Needs You as a 🔔 bell — neither is a place (second ruling, 2026-09-17; app-ux-plan.md §7.7–§7.11).

  • mac-feed.svg — macOS — Feed (home): the six-section sidebar with Work and Knowledge expandable, Pinned, the toolbar 🔔 and ＋
  • mac-needs-you.svg — macOS — Needs You as the bell’s panel over any screen: six answers, snooze, batch, the stale refusal
  • mac-work-board.svg — macOS — Work › Board, reached from the expanded Work group: six columns incl. Addressed to, drags and their refusals
  • mac-project.svg — macOS — Work › Projects: mode chip, the one toggle, rollup, §3.17 confirmation
  • mac-knowledge.svg — macOS — Knowledge: Pages · Search · Inbox as sidebar children, page view with links and backlinks, search results
  • mac-agents.svg — macOS — Agents: presence chips, autonomy level and scope, drag-to-dispatch
  • mac-insights.svg — macOS — Insights: spend over time, run metrics, shadow agreement, token and latency trends (was mac-system.svg)
  • mac-chat.svg — macOS — Chat: collapsed tool activity, prompt card, model and effort picker
  • mac-settings.svg — macOS — Settings: six panes, now including Status, Compute and Devices & Instances
  • mac-wizard.svg — macOS — the setup wizard as a stepper, with “Choose your compute” as the step body
  • mac-menubar.svg — macOS — the app menu, with “Set up…”, beside the menu bar extra: status, quick capture, the Needs You count
  • iphone-feed.svg — iPhone — Feed, with the four-plus-More tab bar, the 🔔 and the floating ＋
  • iphone-triage.svg — iPhone — the request queue as the bell’s sheet: six answers over two rows, swipe actions, the notification
  • iphone-chat.svg — iPhone — Chat: bubbles, the composer menu, inline autocomplete
  • iphone-capture.svg — iPhone — the capture composer as the floating ＋’s sheet, at a medium detent
  • pwa-wide.svg — PWA — wide: the same nav as a six-row sidebar, 🔔 and ＋ in the header
  • pwa-narrow.svg — PWA — narrow, installed: four sections plus More, safe areas
